{"body":"**Context & Current State:**
SSR already works (`pathland-render-html` + `HtmlRenderer`, wired in the Quarkus/Spring demos with `data-pathland-id` hydration). **Semantic landmarks and a real heading hierarchy are now emitted** from the `ROLE` / `TEXT_STYLE` properties: the semantic-only `ROLE` catalog (`MAIN`→`<main>`, `NAVIGATION`→`<nav>`, `BANNER`→`<header>`, `CONTENT_INFO`→`<footer>`, `ARTICLE`, `SECTION`, …) retags generic shells, heading typographies (`TEXT_STYLE` LargeTitle…Headline) produce `<h1>`–`<h5>` with `ROLE_HEADER` defaulting to `<h2>`, and the mapping is pinned by the `pathland-html-golden` conformance harness across both the Rust SSR renderer and the TypeScript DOM client. But the document head is still hardcoded (`<title>Pathland</title>`, generic viewport), and there is no meta/OG/structured data — so initial views lack rich SEO metadata.

**Goal:**
Make the server-rendered document fully crawlable and richly indexed without changing the protocol's declarative model.

**Tasks / Acceptance Criteria:**
- [x] Emit semantic landmarks (`<main>`, `<nav>`, `<header>`/`<footer>`) and a real heading hierarchy from role/heading properties — **done**: semantic-only `ROLE` catalog + `TEXT_STYLE`-driven headings; landmark/heading conformance across Rust SSR + TS DOM client.
- [ ] Add a renderer option/hook to supply `<title>`, description, canonical URL, and Open Graph/Twitter meta per view.
- [ ] Add JSON-LD structured data output (component-type-driven) for indexable content.
- [ ] Add SEO render tests (title/meta/landmark assertions) to both HTML renderers. Landmark assertions already exist in the conformance harness; title/meta assertions will follow with the meta feature.

**Technical Notes / Suggested Approach:**
Extend the `render(root)` API to accept document metadata; keep it a pure function of the opcode stream + metadata (no renderer state). **Last updated:** October 27, 2026

# pathland-html-golden — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 27, 2026

Cross-renderer **golden conformance fixtures** for the HTML renderers.

## Implemented

- A battery of self-contained `PLPL` scenario batches (counter, form,
  composite controls, layout, tokens, **semantics** — semantic roles mapping to
  native elements/ARIA, **icons** — the `ICON` primitive's inline filled (Remix)
  SVG markup carrying `data-pathland-icon` (decorative + labeled, `FONT_SIZE`
  sizing), **sizethatfits** — the `SIZE_THAT_FITS` slot with its selected
  child + `FIT_QUERY` LIST mirrored to `data-pathland-fit`, **media** —
  image alt/content-mode + a `VIDEO` surface bound to its `MEDIA_CONTROLLER`
  (non-visual hidden controller shell), **native_controls** — picker/date/color/
  progress/video native shells carrying their design-system classes,
  **framebounds** — a fill-width frame clamped by `MAX_WIDTH` around a fit slot
  (the player-bar first-paint regression), and a base→delta pair whose change
  includes a `ROLE` change exercising the semantic-tag retag), each rendered by
  the canonical Rust SSR renderer into committed fixtures under
  `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/` (`{name}.plpl` batch bytes + `{name}.html`
  canonical `render_fragment`).
- `--emit` (regenerate fixtures) / `--check` (verify) CLI.
- `tests/guard.rs`: `cargo test -p pathland-html-golden` fails if the committed
  fixtures no longer match the current renderer output.
- The TypeScript DOM client consumes the same fixtures in
  `lib/typescript/test/ssr-conformance.test.ts` (fresh-DOM + hydrate-then-delta),
  so the Rust SSR output is the single contract both renderers must reproduce.

## Regenerate

`cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit` (or `npm run regen` from
`lib/typescript`), then commit the fixtures with the change that produced them.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Scenario coverage is a representative slice (the core shells + tokens); it is
  not exhaustive over every property/component combination.

parts.text:
Now, key design decision: should canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD be passed as renderer options (document metadata) vs protocol. Issue explicitly suggests renderer option/hook. But title/description already from protocol. Need "per view" metadata — since SSR is per request, host knows route and request host; pass options into renderHtml. Also maybe add a host-level "DocumentMetadata" resolution hook (PathlandApp or registry) that receives route and window meta, so title/description etc.

+++ lib/typescript-angular-demo/node_modules/sass/types/compile.d.ts	
@@ -0,0 +1,342 @@
+import {RawSourceMap} from 'source-map-js';
+
+import {Options, StringOptions} from './options';
+
+/**
+ * The result of compiling Sass to CSS. Returned by {@link compile}, {@link
+ * compileAsync}, {@link compileString}, and {@link compileStringAsync}.
+ *
+ * @category Compile
+ */
+export interface CompileResult {
+  /**
+   * The generated CSS.
+   *
+   * Note that this *never* includes a `sourceMapUrl` comment—it's up to the
+   * caller to determine where to save the source map and how to link to it from
+   * the stylesheet.
+   */
+  css: string;
+
+  /**
+   * The canonical URLs of all the stylesheets that were loaded during the
+   * Sass compilation. The order of these URLs is not guaranteed.
+   */
+  loadedUrls: URL[];
+
+  /**
+   * The object representation of the source map that maps locations in the
+   * generated CSS back to locations in the Sass source code.
+   *
+   * This typically uses absolute `file:` URLs to refer to Sass files, although
+   * this can be controlled by having a custom {@link Importer} return {@link
+   * ImporterResult.sourceMapUrl}.
+   *
+   * This is set if and only if {@link Options.sourceMap} is `true`.
+   */
+  sourceMap?: RawSourceMap;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The result of creating a synchronous compiler. Returned by
+ * {@link initCompiler}.
+ *
+ * @category Compile
+ */
+export class Compiler {
+  /**
+   * Throws an error if constructed directly, instead of via
+   * {@link initCompiler}.
+   */
+  private constructor();
+
+  /**
+   * The {@link compile} method exposed through a Compiler instance while it is
+   * active. If this is called after {@link dispose} on the Compiler
+   * instance, an error will be thrown.
+   *
+   * During the Compiler instance's lifespan, given the same input, this will
+   * return an identical result to the {@link compile} method exposed at the
+   * module root.
+   */
+  compile(path: string, options?: Options<'sync'>): CompileResult;
+
+  /**
+   * The {@link compileString} method exposed through a Compiler instance while
+   * it is active. If this is called after {@link dispose} on the Compiler
+   * instance, an error will be thrown.
+   *
+   * During the Compiler instance's lifespan, given the same input, this will
+   * return an identical result to the {@link compileString} method exposed at
+   * the module root.
+   */
+  compileString(source: string, options?: StringOptions<'sync'>): CompileResult;
+
+  /**
+   * Ends the lifespan of this Compiler instance. After this is invoked, all
+   * calls to the Compiler instance's {@link compile} or {@link compileString}
+   * methods will result in an error.
+   */
+  dispose(): void;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The result of creating an asynchronous compiler. Returned by
+ * {@link initAsyncCompiler}.
+ *
+ * @category Compile
+ */
+export class AsyncCompiler {
+  /**
+   * Throws an error if constructed directly, instead of via
+   * {@link initAsyncCompiler}.
+   */
+  private constructor();
+
+  /**
+   * The {@link compileAsync} method exposed through an Async Compiler instance
+   * while it is active. If this is called after {@link dispose} on the Async
+   * Compiler instance, an error will be thrown.
+   *
+   * During the Async Compiler instance's lifespan, given the same input, this
+   * will return an identical result to the {@link compileAsync} method exposed
+   * at the module root.
+   */
+  compileAsync(
+    path: string,
+    options?: Options<'async'>
+  ): Promise<CompileResult>;
+
+  /**
+   * The {@link compileStringAsync} method exposed through an Async Compiler
+   * instance while it is active. If this is called after {@link dispose} on the
+   * Async Compiler instance, an error will be thrown.
+   *
+   * During the Async Compiler instance's lifespan, given the same input, this
+   * will return an identical result to the {@link compileStringAsync} method
+   * exposed at the module root.
+   */
+  compileStringAsync(
+    source: string,
+    options?: StringOptions<'async'>
+  ): Promise<CompileResult>;
+
+  /**
+   * Ends the lifespan of this Async Compiler instance. After this is invoked,
+   * all subsequent calls to the Compiler instance's `compileAsync` or
+   * `compileStringAsync` methods will result in an error.
+   *
+   * Any compilations that are submitted before `dispose` will not be cancelled,
+   * and will be allowed to settle.
+   *
+   * After all compilations have been settled and Sass completes any internal
+   * task cleanup, `dispose` will resolve its promise.
+   */
+  dispose(): Promise<void>;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Synchronously compiles the Sass file at `path` to CSS. If it succeeds it
+ * returns a {@link CompileResult}, and if it fails it throws an {@link
+ * Exception}.
+ *
+ * This only allows synchronous {@link Importer}s and {@link CustomFunction}s.
+ *
+ * **Heads up!** When using the [sass-embedded] npm package for single
+ * compilations, **{@link compileAsync} is almost always faster than
+ * {@link compile}**, due to the overhead of emulating synchronous messaging
+ * with worker threads and concurrent compilations being blocked on main thread.
+ *
+ * If you are running multiple compilations with the [sass-embedded] npm
+ * package, using a {@link Compiler} will provide some speed improvements over
+ * the module-level methods, and an {@link AsyncCompiler} will be much faster.
+ *
+ * [sass-embedded]: https://www.npmjs.com/package/sass-embedded
+ *
+ * @example
+ *
+ * ```js
+ * const sass = require('sass');
+ *
+ * const result = sass.compile("style.scss");
+ * console.log(result.css);
+ * ```
+ *
+ * @category Compile
+ * @compatibility dart: "1.45.0", node: false
+ */
+export function compile(path: string, options?: Options<'sync'>): CompileResult;
+
+/**
+ * Asynchronously compiles the Sass file at `path` to CSS. Returns a promise
+ * that resolves with a {@link CompileResult} if it succeeds and rejects with an
+ * {@link Exception} if it fails.
+ *
+ * This only allows synchronous or asynchronous {@link Importer}s and
+ * {@link CustomFunction}s.
+ *
+ * **Heads up!** When using the `sass` npm package, **{@link compile} is almost
+ * twice as fast as {@link compileAsync}**, due to the overhead of making the
+ * entire evaluation process asynchronous.
+ *
+ * @example
+ *
+ * ```js
+ * const sass = require('sass');
+ *
+ * const result = await sass.compileAsync("style.scss");

+ *   }

+ *
+ * [sass]: https://www.npmjs.com/package/sass
+ *

+ *
+ * ```js

+ * @compatibility dart: "1.70.0", node: false
+ */

   - `mainEntityOfPage`: canonical
   - `url`: canonical
3. Maybe for ROLE == MAIN with no Article: not needed.
4. Structured data only for indexable content: enabled by option `jsonLd = true` (default false? or true when title/description?). The acceptance says "Add JSON-LD structured data output ... for indexable content." I'd make it opt-in via DocumentMetadata (default off) to avoid surprising payloads, or auto-on when canonical provided. Better explicit `structuredData(true)`.

Need know IMAGE source property ID.

# pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 6, 2026

The **pure-Java HTML renderer** (`dev.pathland.render.html`) — a behavioural
port of the Rust `pathland-render-html` crate. Stateless: each call decodes a
self-contained snapshot frame into a transient tree and renders it to HTML in
one pass. No JNA and no cdylib, so a Maven dependency runs on every platform and
is GraalVM native-image compatible (no reachability/resource config for a native
library). Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Pure-Java renderer**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` / `tryInstance()` /
  `isAvailable()` (always true); `render(frame, root)` /
  `renderFragment(frame, root)` / `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a
  self-contained snapshot in one pass. The public API is unchanged from the
  former JNA shim, so `PathlandSession`, Spring, and Quarkus need no changes.
- **Byte-identical Rust output**: `GoldenConformanceTest` renders every
  committed `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/*.plpl` fixture and compares the
  fragment to its `.html` fixture byte-for-byte (the same contract the TS DOM
  client asserts), including the delta base/change/result scenario.
- **Full renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render inline
  (structural + decorative CSS in a single `style` attribute), ARIA/event
  attributes, `IS_SECURE` → password, `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants,
  `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, literal colors inline, attributed text, media
  surfaces/controllers, proxy views, grid rows/tracks, fit bands, and
  size-that-fits snapshots.
- **Built-in base design**: the generated `design/build/base.css` (synced into
  the Rust assets) is copied into the jar at build time and inlined by the
  default `render(...)`. `renderLinked(frame, root, cssBase)` /
  `renderLinkedDebug(...)` emit a content-hashed
  `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{cssBase}/{baseCssName()}">`; `baseCss()` /
  `baseCssName()` expose the renderer-owned bytes for immutable serving.
- **Debug comments**: `renderDebug` / `renderFragmentDebug` prefix every node
  with an HTML comment naming its component and decoded modifiers.
- **Icon glyphs**: `iconSvg(name)` returns the full inline `<svg>` for a
  canonical `ICON_NAME` (unknown names → the fallback glyph; `null` → `null`),
  so hosts serve `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from the same table SSR inlines.
- **Demos use the renderer**: the Spring Boot and Quarkus starters SSR through
  `HtmlRenderer`, and the DOM client hydrates in place.

## Not implemented / gaps

- **Typography uses the platform system font stack**; the document head makes no
  external/webfont requests.
- The renderer is a port of the Rust implementation, not a second source of
  truth: when the HTML output changes, update the Rust crate + golden fixtures
  and this port together (`GoldenConformanceTest` fails on drift).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-render-html` — the golden conformance suite plus the
DSL → emitter → frame → renderer round-trip tests. Part of the non-demo reactor
run on JDK 17/21/25 and under GraalVM native-image.

parts.text:
User wants app to change meta dynamically based on route; first SSR rendering contains it. That means app-level hook is needed (or dynamic metadata via signals/protocol). Since canonical/OG are host concerns but app needs per-route dynamic. We need design that lets app define metadata per route and have it available during SSR before render. Options:

1. Add app-level method `PageMetadata pageMetadata(String route)` to PathlandApp. Registry/session calls it after environment route is set (before rendering), so route-aware. The host controller passes canonical URL separately, or app receives canonical URL too? Canonical requires request URL; could pass canonical URL to hook. But route alone can build path; canonical origin needs host. Design:
   - `PathlandApp` default method:
     ```java
     default PageMetadata pageMetadata(PageMetadataContext context) { return PageMetadata.none(); }
     ```
     Context has `route` (mount-stripped), `canonicalUrl` (host-built, or null), maybe initial environment/viewport? At SSR time.
   - Registry's `renderHtml(route, windowId, canonicalUrl)` builds context, calls app hook. The returned metadata merges with host-level defaults/config.
   - Or `PathlandApp.documentMeta(String route, String canonicalUrl)` returning a neutral `PageMetadata`.
   - In Spring/Quarkus, the app implements it; e.g. MusicPlayerView maybe returns title/description? But title/description already window metadata. For canonical/OG/JSON-LD type, app route hook can return `og:type=article`, image, etc.
   - For dynamic per route, route is known at SSR because request path seeds Environment ROUTE before mount. Also the app view can set window metadata signals, which are emitted then decoded by renderer. For other meta (canonical/OG image), hook returns values.

2. Alternatively, protocol extension: add `CANONICAL`, `IMAGE`, `SITE_NAME`, etc. to `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA`, so app sets dynamically and renderer maps. But spec says canonical is host concern, web-only artifacts not protocol fields. User explicitly wants app-driven dynamic metadata. We could add fields like `IMAGE` and `OG_TYPE` not canonical? But canonical is fundamentally a URL, host can derive. Yet app may need to define per route. Could add `CANONICAL_PATH` or `ROUTE`-derived. Hmm.

User's answer says "Must be able for the app to change meta dynamically. Based on fx. path a specific route may be activated and then the metadata could be defined by it so the first SSR rendering contains it." This strongly suggests app-level hook (or protocol). Since app knows route at SSR, a hook is natural. It also means title/description are already protocol and dynamic; canonical/OG/JSON-LD need route-based app control.

We need design a `PageMetadata` hook:
- Where to put it? `PathlandApp` is the app factory. Add default method:
  ```java
  default PageMetadata pageMetadata(PageMetadataContext context) {
      return PageMetadata.empty();
  }
  ```
  This keeps host compatibility.
- `PageMetadataContext`: record with `String route`, `String canonicalUrl`, maybe `Environment`? The app may want route params; route string enough. Could include `String mountPath`? Route is stripped. Could include request? No, transport-agnostic. Maybe include `Map<String,String>`? no.
- `PageMetadata`: neutral class in server-core (not renderer module) with fields title, description, canonicalUrl, siteName, imageUrl, ogType, twitterCard, twitterSite, structuredData. But renderer `DocumentMeta` has same fields. Could make renderer `DocumentMeta` the shared type and have server-core depend on render-html (already does). But `PathlandApp` in server-core referencing renderer DTO is okay? It already depends on renderer for session. But app module (demo views Kotlin) might not depend on renderer? PathlandApp is server-core; demo views depend on view-core, not server-core. The app implementation (QuarkusDemoApp) depends on server-core. So okay. Still, cleaner: keep `PageMetadata` in server-core, convert to `DocumentMeta` in session. But duplicate classes. Alternatively move `DocumentMeta` to `pathland-render-core`? But render-html is independent. Java renderer module shouldn't depend on server-core. So `DocumentMeta` in render-html and `PageMetadata` in server-core with conversion. Or put `DocumentMeta` in server-core and render-html accepts a generic? No.

Could have `PathlandApp` return `dev.pathland.render.html.DocumentMeta` directly; server-core already imports HtmlRenderer. But this couples app to renderer implementation. Acceptable? Maybe. The repo's app hosts already include server-core, which exposes renderer classes as an implementation detail. I'd lean neutral `PageMetadata` in server-core (transport-agnostic) to avoid leaking renderer module. But then hosts map to renderer `DocumentMeta`. It's a small mapping.

Alternative: Add fields to the protocol window metadata. Let's reconsider. `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` is extensible. AGENTS/spec says web-only artifacts canonical/robots/sitemap are host concerns and not protocol fields. But Open Graph image/type/site are arguably presentation metadata akin to title/description; canonical is web-only. User specifically wants dynamic meta per route, but title/description already dynamic; for canonical, host can compute from route; OG image/type could be app-driven. If we add `IMAGE`, `TYPE`, `SITE_NAME`, `TWITTER_*` to protocol, all renderers need mapping and the spec changes. But canonical still host-only (derived). That might be cleaner for dynamic app control and "first SSR rendering contains it": app emits these via view modifiers, engine emits in frame, renderer reads them. We would need wire IDs and DSL modifiers, engine propagation, all three renderers, tests. That's much larger than issue scope, and contradicts "web-only artifacts are host concerns". The issue technical notes explicitly say extend render API with document metadata. So don't extend protocol.

Thus app hook is right. Need route-based hook and how canonical is supplied. Design:

- `PathlandApp` gains:
  ```java
  default PageMetadata pageMetadata(String route) { return PageMetadata.empty(); }
  ```
  But canonical URL not available to app. We can have the host pass canonical separately and let app set only app-specific fields; canonical auto = request URL. If app wants to override canonical (e.g., canonical points to another route), it can set `canonicalUrl` in PageMetadata; host wins if app returns null. So:
  - `PageMetadata` fields with nullable values; `canonicalUrl` optional override.
  - Registry/session computes canonical URL (passed from controller) and merges: app values > host defaults > derived canonical.
  - App hook receives route and maybe the derived canonical:
    ```java
    default PageMetadata pageMetadata(String route, String canonicalUrl)
    ```
    The app can use canonical to build absolute OG image URLs. This is useful.
- Title/description: app might also return them as fallbacks; META wins.
- JSON-LD `structuredData` bool: host default true; app can disable for non-indexable routes (e.g., player).
- `ogType`: app returns "article" for article routes; "website" default.
- `imageUrl`: app returns absolute/relative; if relative and canonical available, resolve.
- `siteName`, `twitterCard`, `twitterSite`: host config defaults; app overrides.

Where is hook called? In `PathlandRegistry.renderHtml` before creating session? The hook might need the app's route-aware logic but not the view. It has route. The session creates root view and emits. We can call app hook in registry:
```java
PageMetadata page = app.pageMetadata(stripRoute(route), canonicalUrl);
session.renderHtml(serviceWorker, scoped, page);
```
But the app may want window metadata (title) as computed by view; it can still return static route metadata. Fine.
- For live sessions (WebSocket), metadata changes on navigation? The issue is SSR only. But app route navigation in browser: SSR on each full page load; client navigation won't update OG. Could later use WS to send metadata; out of scope. Maybe mention.
- The app hook can be called for SSR only, not live sessions. `PathlandSession.renderHtml` gets `PageMetadata`.

But `PathlandApp` is a functional interface `View newRoot()`. Adding a default method keeps lambdas valid. Good.

Host controllers still need to pass canonical URL:
- Change `PathlandRegistry.renderHtml(route, windowId, canonicalUrl)` or a metadata context. The app hook needs canonical. Add overload:
  ```java
  public String renderHtml(String route, String windowId, String canonicalUrl)
  ```
  Existing overloads pass null. It builds `PageMetadata` via `app.pageMetadata(stripRoute(route), canonicalUrl)` and host defaults from `PathlandSeo` config.
- `PathlandHost`/registry needs `PathlandSeo` config (siteName, image, twitterSite, ogType, structuredData, enabled). Could be passed to registry constructors; or build only in controllers and pass full PageMetadata. But app hook lives in registry. Add a `PageMetadataResolver` or `SeoDefaults` to registry. Simplest: registry constructor takes `SeoConfig` (new class) defaulting to enabled/seo. PathlandHost constructors take SeoConfig; Spring/Quarkus configs build it. That's a lot of constructor changes. Alternatively add a `Function<PageMetadataContext, PageMetadata> pageMetadataResolver` in registry, composed by host. But host defaults plus app hook.

Maybe simpler:
- `PathlandApp` default method gets `PageMetadataContext` (route, canonicalUrl, host defaults?). It can return metadata. Host controllers build host defaults and pass full `PageMetadata` to registry; registry calls app hook to allow overrides. Merge:
  ```java
  PageMetadata base = host supplied (config+canonical)
  PageMetadata appMeta = app.pageMetadata(context)
  base.merge(appMeta) // app wins
  ```
- Spring controller holds `@Value` config and constructs base; Quarkus same. No need to thread config through host constructors. But duplication in both starters and any custom host. Could put a helper in server-core `PageMetadata.fromConfig(canonicalUrl, enabled, siteName, image, twitterSite, ogType, jsonLd)`.

But `PathlandApp.pageMetadata` should be part of the contract, and custom hosts can call `registry.renderHtml(route, wid, canonicalUrl)`; registry builds base with defaults (enabled, no site info) and app hook. Host-specific config still needed for siteName etc. A `PageMetadataContext` could include `canonicalUrl`. The app can supply siteName too. In demos, set siteName in the app hook. That removes need for config in host? But the issue says configurable. Add config in starters as base, merged with app hook.

Let me propose:
- `PageMetadata` (server-core neutral) with nullable fields + `enabled` maybe.
- `PageMetadataRequest` context record `(String route, String canonicalUrl, String mountPath)`.
- `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(PageMetadataRequest request)` default `PageMetadata.empty()`.
- `PathlandRegistry.renderHtml(String route, String windowId, String canonicalUrl)`:
  1. build `PageMetadataRequest` with stripped route + canonical + mount.
  2. `PageMetadata fromApp = app.pageMetadata(request)`.
  3. Merge with registry-level `PageMetadata defaults` (configured by host) → app overrides.
  4. Convert to renderer `DocumentMeta` and pass to session.renderHtml.
- Add a registry-level `PageMetadata defaults` field + setter/constructor:
  - `PathlandRegistry.setSeoDefaults(PageMetadata)`? Registries built in PathlandHost; host constructor could accept defaults. But simpler: `PathlandHost`/`PathlandRegistry` gets `SeoDefaults` from starters. We can add a `PageMetadata defaults` constructor param with a default no-arg. This is API growth; need to preserve existing constructors.
  - Or controllers can pass `PageMetadata hostDefaults` into `renderHtml(route, wid, canonicalUrl)`? Registry doesn't need config then; controller builds defaults. But then app hook merge happens in registry. Signature: `renderHtml(route, wid, canonicalUrl, PageMetadata hostDefaults)`. A bit ugly.
  - Better: `renderHtml(route, wid, PageMetadataRequest request, PageMetadata hostDefaults)`. Hmm.

Maybe avoid host-level config in registry and let the app hook own all metadata. The starters provide a default `PageMetadata` only via a `PathlandSeo` bean that the controller reads. The controller builds `PageMetadata base = seo.resolve(requestUrl)` and calls `registry.renderHtml(route, wid, base)`. Registry merges app hook. App hook gets route+canonical. This is clean:
  - `PathlandRegistry.renderHtml(String route, String windowId, PageMetadata baseMetadata)`; if null, default `PageMetadata.enabled()` maybe with canonical null.
  - Controller computes `baseMetadata` from config and canonical URL.
  - Registry constructs `PageMetadataRequest` and calls app hook, merges app over base.
  - Existing `renderHtml(route, wid)` calls `renderHtml(route, wid, PageMetadata.defaults())` (canonical null) — no SEO output unless base requests it. But if we want canonical by default, controller always passes base with canonical.
- Starters:
  - `PathlandSeoProperties` (Spring) / config in Quarkus: `pathland.seo.enabled` (true), `site-name`, `image`, `twitter-site`, `og-type`, `json-ld` (true). Build `base = PageMetadata.seo(canonicalUrl).siteName(...).image(...)` etc. If disabled, `PageMetadata.empty()`.
  - Controller passes base to registry.
- App hook can override `ogType`, image, canonical, title/description fallback, structuredData, and disable.

This supports dynamic per-route app metadata. Title/description still via protocol (META) and takes precedence. Great.

Question: Should `PageMetadata` include canonical URL derived by app? If app returns canonical, it overrides host canonical. Yes.

Should app hook be evaluated before or after root view render? Route is enough. If app needs view-derived values beyond window metadata, no. Fine.

Need update `PathlandApp` javadoc and tests.

Now, dynamic metadata via signals: Title/description bound to signals update live via META, so SSR with route-seeded environment has correct values. Good.

Could also let app return metadata per route by inspecting route. Demo: In `QuarkusDemoApp`/`SpringDemoApplication` return a `PathlandApp` lambda? They currently return view. To use default method with lambda impossible (lambdas only implement abstract method, can't override default). Users would create an anonymous class or a class implementing PathlandApp. The demos' `PathlandApp` bean can be an anonymous class overriding `newRoot` and `pageMetadata`. Fine. # Plan: Issue #45 — SEO-hardened SSR

## Decisions (from your answers)

- **Protocol stays unchanged.** Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are renderer/host concerns (spec/OPCODE.md:534-536). Title, description, and locale continue to come from `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA`.
- **App-driven per-route metadata** is required, so the app can define metadata from the active route before the first SSR paint.
- Structured data: **WebPage + Article** (Article derived from `ROLE_ARTICLE`).
- Starters emit SEO head by default, configurable via `pathland.seo.*`.
- Rust C ABI gets a flat meta struct for non-JVM hosts.

## Current state

- Head is built in exactly two places:
  - Rust: `render_document_with_head` at `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/lib.rs:1391`
  - Java: `renderDocument` at `lib/java/pathland-render-html/src/main/java/dev/pathland/render/html/HtmlRenderer.java:364`
- Both already map `TITLE` → `<title>`, `DESCRIPTION` → meta description, `LOCALE` → `<html lang>`.
- Semantic landmarks/headings are done.
- No canonical, OG, Twitter, or JSON-LD anywhere.
- SSR flows through `PathlandRegistry.renderHtml` → `PathlandSession.renderHtml`.
- The golden harness only compares fragments; there is no document-head cross-renderer fixture.
- Spec already says canonical/robots/sitemap are host-owned, not protocol fields (`spec/OPCODE.md:534`).

---

## 1. Rust renderer: `DocumentMeta` option + SEO head

New files:
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/document.rs`
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/structured_data.rs`

`DocumentMeta` (builder-style, pure value, no renderer state):

```rust
pub struct DocumentMeta {
    title: Option<String>,          // fallback; META TITLE wins
    description: Option<String>,    // fallback; META DESCRIPTION wins
    canonical_url: Option<String>,
    site_name: Option<String>,
    image_url: Option<String>,
    og_type: Option<String>,        // default "website"
    twitter_card: Option<String>,   // default summary / summary_large_image
    twitter_site: Option<String>,
    open_graph: bool,
    twitter: bool,
    structured_data: bool,
}
```

Public API additions in `lib.rs`:
- `render_document_with_meta(opcodes, strings, root, &DocumentMeta)`
- `render_document_linked_with_meta(opcodes, strings, root, css_base, &DocumentMeta)`
- Existing methods delegate with `DocumentMeta::none()` so current output/fixtures stay unchanged.

Head emission:
- Effective title/description: `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` value first, then `DocumentMeta` fallback.
- Canonical: `<link rel="canonical" href="...">` when `canonical_url` is present.
- OG when enabled: `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:type`, `og:url`, `og:site_name`, `og:image`, `og:locale`.
- Twitter when enabled: `twitter:card`, `twitter:title`, `twitter:description`, `twitter:image`, `twitter:site`.
- `og:image` / `twitter:image`: explicit `image_url`, else the first `IMAGE` source in the tree; resolve root-relative paths against the canonical origin when possible.
- All attribute values use the existing HTML escaper.

JSON-LD (`structured_data.rs`):
- Emit only when `structured_data` is enabled and there is something meaningful to describe.
- Build a deterministic `@graph`:
  - `WebPage`: `name`, `description`, `url`, `inLanguage`.
  - One `Article` per `ROLE_ARTICLE` node (document order): `headline` = first heading descendant, `description` = first paragraph descendant, `image` = first `IMAGE` source, `mainEntityOfPage` = canonical, `inLanguage`.
- Fixed key order so Rust and Java can be byte-identical.
- JSON escaping must HTML-safe-escape `<`, `>`, `&`, U+2028/U+2029 and normal JSON control characters so app text cannot break out of `<script type="application/ld+json">`.

Tests in the Rust crate:
- canonical/OG/Twitter exact head output
- fallback precedence (`META` wins over `DocumentMeta`)
- JSON-LD WebPage + Article extraction
- script-breakout escaping
- no `DocumentMeta` → byte-identical legacy head

## 2. C ABI parity

In `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/capi.rs`:
- Add `#[repr(C)] PathlandHtmlMeta` with nullable `*const c_char` fields + `u8` enable flags.
- Add `pathland_html_render_with_meta(batch, len, root, css_base, meta, debug)`.
- Keep existing functions unchanged.
- Add C-ABI tests for null meta and populated meta.

## 3. Java renderer parity

New files under `lib/java/pathland-render-html/src/main/java/dev/pathland/render/html/`:
- `DocumentMeta.java`
- `StructuredData.java` (or add JSON helpers to `Format.java`)

`HtmlRenderer` additions:
- `render(frame, root, DocumentMeta)`
- `renderLinked(frame, root, cssBase, DocumentMeta)`
- `renderLinkedDebug(...)`, `renderDebug(...)` overloads
- Existing methods delegate to `DocumentMeta.none()`
- Refactor `renderDocument` to accept `DocumentMeta` and reuse the same tag construction order as Rust.

Tests:
- `HtmlRendererTest` / new `DocumentMetaTest.kt`:
  - title/meta/landmark assertions for both inline and linked docs
  - canonical/OG/Twitter
  - JSON-LD WebPage + Article
  - escaping/script-breakout

## 4. App-driven per-route metadata in server-core

New types in `lib/java/pathland-server-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/server/`:
- `PageMetadata` — neutral transport-agnostic metadata value:
  - nullable `title`, `description`, `canonicalUrl`, `siteName`, `imageUrl`, `ogType`, `twitterCard`, `twitterSite`
  - nullable `Boolean` flags for openGraph/twitter/structuredData
  - `overlay(base)` merge helper
- `PageMetadataRequest` — `route`, `canonicalUrl`, `mountPath`.

`PathlandApp` (`PathlandApp.java`):
- Add a default method, preserving functional-interface compatibility:

```java
default PageMetadata pageMetadata(PageMetadataRequest request) {
    return PageMetadata.empty();
}
```

This is the route-aware hook: the app sees the active, mount-stripped route during SSR and can return route-specific canonical/OG type/image/etc.

`PathlandRegistry`:
- Add `renderHtml(String route, String windowId, PageMetadata hostDefaults)`.
- Existing overloads delegate with `PageMetadata.empty()`.
- Flow:
  1. Build `PageMetadataRequest(stripRoute(route), canonicalUrl, mountPath)`.
  2. Call `app.pageMetadata(request)`.
  3. Merge host defaults ← app metadata (app wins).
  4. Convert to renderer `DocumentMeta` and pass into `PathlandSession`.
- No protocol/session-state change; this is SSR-only metadata, consistent with renderer statelessness.

`PathlandSession`:
- Add `renderHtml(boolean serviceWorker, boolean ssrScoped, DocumentMeta meta)`.
- Existing methods delegate with `DocumentMeta.none()`.

## 5. Starter integration

### Spring Boot
- `PathlandIndexController`:
  - Build canonical from the request URL without query string (`request.getRequestURL()`, not `wID`/query).
  - Build host-default `PageMetadata` from config.
  - Pass it to `registry.renderHtml(route, wid, metadata)`.
- Config keys with safe defaults:
  - `pathland.seo.enabled=true`
  - `pathland.seo.structured-data=true`
  - `pathland.seo.site-name=`
  - `pathland.seo.image=`
  - `pathland.seo.og-type=website`
  - `pathland.seo.twitter-card=`
  - `pathland.seo.twitter-site=`

### Quarkus
- `IndexResource`:
  - Inject `@Context UriInfo` into `index`/`deep`/`render`.
  - Canonical = request URI with query removed.
  - Same `pathland.seo.*` config keys via `@ConfigProperty`.
  - Pass `PageMetadata` to the registry.

### Demos
- Implement `pageMetadata(...)` in the demo `PathlandApp`s (Spring and Quarkus).
  - Example: default website metadata; `/kotlin` route-specific description/OG type.
  - The player route can stay `og:type=website`; article-like routes can return `article`.
- Add demo `application.properties` SEO defaults (site name, optional image/twitter handle).

## 6. Golden conformance + docs

- Extend `pathland-html-golden`:
  - Add a `document_meta` scenario containing WebPage content + an `ROLE_ARTICLE` subtree (heading, paragraph, image).
  - Emit `document_meta.plpl` + `document_meta.document.html` using `render_document_with_meta`.
  - Update `check`/`emit` so the document fixture is guarded.
- Add a Java `DocumentGoldenConformanceTest` comparing the Java renderer against `document_meta.document.html` byte-for-byte.
- TypeScript conformance can ignore `.document.html` (head is not hydrated by the DOM client); no TS renderer change needed.
- Update `status.md` in mandatory places:
  - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/status.md`
  - `lib/java/pathland-render-html/status.md`
  - `lib/java/pathland-server-core/status.md`
  - Spring Boot / Quarkus / demo statuses as applicable
- Add a short note to the renderer docs/README: SEO head is host/renderer metadata, not protocol. Optionally add one clarifying sentence in `spec/OPCODE.md` near the window-metadata section; no ID changes.

## 7. Test plan

Rust:
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo test -p pathland-render-html -p pathland-html-golden`
- `cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit` (once) then commit fixtures
- `cargo test` workspace

Java:
- `cd lib/java && mvn -pl pathland-render-html,pathland-server-core,pathland-spring-boot-starter,pathland-quarkus -am test`
- `mvn install` for the full reactor

JS:
- `cd lib/typescript && npm test` (existing fragment conformance must remain green)

Manual:
- Run Spring and Quarkus demos, `curl -s http://localhost:.../` and verify:
  - `<title>`, description, `<html lang>`
  - canonical link
  - OG/Twitter tags
  - `<script type="application/ld+json">` containing WebPage/Article
  - `<main>`, `<nav>`, heading hierarchy
- Verify a route with app-specific metadata (e.g. `/kotlin`) gets its route-defined values on the first response.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- Updating canonical/OG tags during client-side SPA navigation after the initial SSR (title/description already update over `META`; canonical/OG would need a new mechanism).
- Sitemap/robots changes — already host-owned and existing.
- Adding canonical/OG fields to `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` — intentionally avoided to keep web-only artifacts out of the protocol.
- Richer structured data (BreadcrumbList, Organization, ImageObject, per-article URLs) beyond the agreed WebPage + Article scope.

   `frameworkFile` path) serves the renderer-owned content-hashed base design
   (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
   `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. **`/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg`**
   serves the renderer-owned icon glyphs from the shared Rust renderer
   (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` → `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache
   header — no static CSS/icon files on any host. SSR links the CSS via
   `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.

   `MountedApp` bean plus the lone `PathlandApp` bean (mounted at `/`); `@Disposes` shuts
   it down. Reads the `pathland.debug-html` config property (default `false`) to enable
   per-node HTML comments in SSR output, and `pathland.service-worker` (default `false`)
   to opt the DOM client into the per-window-id service worker (issue #155) — served at
   `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`.

   `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so the client's root-scoped
   registration succeeds. A `Filters` handler always runs before routes, so it wins over
   Quarkus's static-resource handler (which sends neither header, and whose configured
   max-age would otherwise cache the script and delay update detection). The script is
   resolved through the thread-context classloader first, then the extension's own
   loader, then the system loader: extension runtime classes live in Quarkus's base
   runtime classloader and cannot see the application's `META-INF/resources` copy. The
   extension jar bundles the worker as a fallback (the TS copy script writes it), and
   `pathland-quarkus-demo`'s integration test asserts the headers on both the root and a
   mounted base — the packaged-app classloader path the module-local test could not see.

   `quarkus-smallrye-health`: the producer builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over the
   registry and decorates it with `TracingTelemetry` when a `Tracer` bean is present and
   `quarkus.otel.enabled` (default `true`; the extension never touches the OTel API when
   the extension is absent/disabled). `PathlandHealthCheck` (`@Readiness`) reports the
   host UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/q/health`; the `pathland.*` meters appear
   at `/q/metrics`.
 - **`QuarkusConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketConnection` to `PathlandConnection`.
   Sends are **serialized** (one `sendBinary` subscription in flight, the rest queued),
   and a **send failure closes the connection** so the session drops it and the DOM
   client reconnects + `META::RESYNC` (recoverable) instead of silently stalling on an
   "open" socket that never delivers (the remote seekbar symptom). **Send timeout**: a
   `sendBinary` that neither completes nor fails within 10 s (a half-dead connection /
   a dropped proxy upstream leg) is marked failed and closed — a hung send would
   otherwise wedge the serialized drain forever. **Keep-alive pings**: the connection
   sends a WS-protocol ping every 15 s (browsers auto-pong) to keep the connection warm
   through middleboxes and detect a dead client; `close()` stops the keep-alive
   scheduler (the sockets' `@OnClose` calls it).

   **at the transport layer** (through their `QuarkusConnection`, no actor/session
   dependency, and a PING never creates or wakes a session); spec/OPCODE.md
   §Transport heartbeat.
 - **Failure handling** — `fail()` logs the reason; `close()` (socket `@OnClose`)
   no longer calls `close()` on the already-closed connection (no spurious
   "Connection already closed" noise). A **transient write failure on a connection
   that still reports open is logged, not closed** — only a confirmed-dead channel
   (or a send hung past the timeout) warrants closing. The send-timeout task is
   **cancelled when the send completes**, so a completed-but-late callback can't
   false-time-out and kill a healthy connection. Keep-alive pings are sent directly
   (Vert.x serializes writes — no sync with `sendBinary` needed).
 - `META-INF/beans.xml` so Quarkus discovers the extension.
 - **Quarkus extension metadata** — runtime + `pathland-quarkus-deployment`; the
   runtime provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus` capability. The runtime has no
   dependency on the authoring DSL. Tests use Kotlin-authored fixture views to prove
   a Java CDI bean can mount them.

 # pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 6, 2026
 
 The **pure-Java HTML renderer** (`dev.pathland.render.html`) — a behavioural
 port of the Rust `pathland-render-html` crate. Stateless: each call decodes a
 self-contained snapshot frame into a transient tree and renders it to HTML in
 one pass. No JNA and no cdylib, so a Maven dependency runs on every platform and
 is GraalVM native-image compatible (no reachability/resource config for a native
 library). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Pure-Java renderer**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` / `tryInstance()` /
   `isAvailable()` (always true); `render(frame, root)` /
   `renderFragment(frame, root)` / `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a
   self-contained snapshot in one pass. The public API is unchanged from the
   former JNA shim, so `PathlandSession`, Spring, and Quarkus need no changes.
 - **Byte-identical Rust output**: `GoldenConformanceTest` renders every
   committed `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/*.plpl` fixture and compares the
   fragment to its `.html` fixture byte-for-byte (the same contract the TS DOM
   client asserts), including the delta base/change/result scenario.
+- **SEO document metadata (issue #45)**: `DocumentMeta`/`render(frame, root,
+  meta)` / `renderLinked(..., meta)` add canonical URL, Open Graph/Twitter
+  cards, and component-derived JSON-LD (WebPage + Article for `ROLE_ARTICLE`).
+  Window `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION` win; the metadata values are fallbacks. The
+  document output is pinned byte-for-byte against the Rust renderer's
+  `document_meta.document.html` fixture.
 - **Full renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render inline
   (structural + decorative CSS in a single `style` attribute), ARIA/event
   attributes, `IS_SECURE` → password, `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants,
   `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, literal colors inline, attributed text, media
   surfaces/controllers, proxy views, grid rows/tracks, fit bands, and
   size-that-fits snapshots.
 - **Built-in base design**: the generated `design/build/base.css` (synced into
   the Rust assets) is copied into the jar at build time and inlined by the
   default `render(...)`. `renderLinked(frame, root, cssBase)` /
   `renderLinkedDebug(...)` emit a content-hashed
   `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{cssBase}/{baseCssName()}">`; `baseCss()` /
   `baseCssName()` expose the renderer-owned bytes for immutable serving.
 - **Debug comments**: `renderDebug` / `renderFragmentDebug` prefix every node
   with an HTML comment naming its component and decoded modifiers.
 - **Icon glyphs**: `iconSvg(name)` returns the full inline `<svg>` for a
   canonical `ICON_NAME` (unknown names → the fallback glyph; `null` → `null`),
   so hosts serve `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from the same table SSR inlines.
 - **Demos use the renderer**: the Spring Boot and Quarkus starters SSR through
   `HtmlRenderer`, and the DOM client hydrates in place.
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - **Typography uses the platform system font stack**; the document head makes no
   external/webfont requests.
 - The renderer is a port of the Rust implementation, not a second source of
   truth: when the HTML output changes, update the Rust crate + golden fixtures
   and this port together (`GoldenConformanceTest` fails on drift).
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `mvn test -pl pathland-render-html` — the golden conformance suite plus the
 DSL → emitter → frame → renderer round-trip tests. Part of the non-demo reactor
 run on JDK 17/21/25 and under GraalVM native-image.

The host's frames feed the session's `DeltaBatcher` (a single unified sequence); `dispatch` splits proxy-range events to the origin and everything else to the app's own bindings; `close` tears the proxies down. `proxyTransportFactory(...)` lets a host supply a framework transport. - **`PathlandTelemetry`** — `proxyConnected`/`proxyDisconnected`/`proxyBatchDropped`/ `proxyResyncRequested` (all default no-ops). **SSR embed (M2).** `renderHtml` starts the proxies and **blocks** for each origin's snapshot (`ProxySession.awaitSnapshot`, bounded by a 2s timeout), then splices the remapped origin frames into the session's mount frame (`FrameMerger`, reusing the batcher's string rebasing via `FrameRebase`) so the renderer emits **one** document — the origin subtree plus its fit band rules in the same head. The origin's **global** token overrides (`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`) are **dropped** (live + SSR): a proxied app renders under the **host's** theme, while its token *references* resolve against that theme (spec/PROXY.md §9). A proxy whose origin does not answer in time renders empty (a placeholder) and hydrates over the live connection. A client `META::RESYNC` also replays A's tree **and** asks every origin for a fresh snapshot (`ProxyHost.resyncAll`). **Gaps (M3):** nested proxies and per-proxy theme scoping are deferred (the origin's global overrides are dropped, not scoped, spec/PROXY.md §9). A tiny orphan window remains on removal: an origin batch already queued in the `DeltaBatcher` (≤20 ms) when the proxy node is removed can still create an unattached element in the client's `byId` (not in the DOM); eliminating it needs the `ProxySession` to track the ids it emitted and `DELETE` them on close. ##  # pathland-spring-boot-starter — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 6, 2026
 
 Spring Boot auto-configuration for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
 app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding the starter dependency + a
 `PathlandApp` bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at their own
 subpaths (the BFF layout).
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Security hardening (issue #63)**: the WebSocket handlers no longer hardcode
   `setAllowedOrigins("*")`. The default is Spring's same-origin handshake check
   (the WebSocket CSRF control); cross-origin hosts must be listed explicitly in
   `pathland.allowed-origins` (comma-separated). The handshake `wid` is validated
   by server-core (`WindowIds`). SSR inherits SRI (`integrity="sha384-…"`) from
   `PathlandSession`. CSP/security headers and transport limits are documented in
   `docs/HARDENING.md` (Quarkus supplies secure defaults; Spring apps add them
   through Spring Security/server configuration).
 - **Java host / Kotlin views**: `KotlinViewMountTest` proves a Java-only
   `@SpringBootApplication` bean returning `PathlandApp` mounts a Kotlin-authored
   fixture view, renders it through SSR, and receives a live signal delta.
 
 - **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.
+- **SEO document head (issue #45)**: the SSR controller derives the canonical
+  URL from the request and passes host-default `PageMetadata` to the registry;
+  `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...)` may override it per route before the first
+  paint. Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are on by default and configurable via
+  `pathland.seo.{enabled,site-name,image,og-type,twitter-card,twitter-site,structured-data}`.
 
 - **`PathlandAutoConfiguration`** (`@AutoConfiguration`, `@EnableWebSocket` since Spring
   Boot 3.5 no longer auto-enables it) + `META-INF/spring/…/AutoConfiguration.imports`:
   - default `StateStore` bean (`@ConditionalOnMissingBean` — Redis-or-in-memory),
   - `PathlandHost` bean (shut down with the context): every `MountedApp` bean plus the
     lone `PathlandApp` bean mounted at `/` (unless an explicit `MountedApp` claims the
     root). Without any app the host is empty and the starter is inert.
   - a `WebSocketConfigurer` registering **one handler per app** at its framework base
     (`/_pathland/ws` for the root, `/{mount}/_pathland/ws` otherwise). Each connection
     gets a fresh `uiId` (its UI model) + the client's `wid` (per-window state scope)
     from the WS `?wid=` query param (kept in `sessionStorage`, never in the page URL),
   - `PathlandIndexController` (SSR catch-all dispatching to the longest-mount app with
     the prefix stripped + a framework static controller serving the bundle + asset mount
     from `classpath:/static/_pathland/**` at both `/_pathland/**` and `/{app}/_pathland/**`;
     the more-specific mapping beats `/{*path}`, and the `!Upgrade` header excludes WS).
     When no static file matches, the controller serves renderer-owned assets from the
     shared Rust renderer: the content-hashed base stylesheet
     (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
     `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and
     `/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg` glyphs (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` →
     `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache header — no static CSS/icon
     files on any host, and a host can still override either with a file. SSR links
     the CSS via `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
     The framework controller honors byte-range requests (`206 Partial Content` +
     `Content-Range`, `416` for unsatisfiable ranges, `Accept-Ranges` on the full
     response) — a `<video>` (a `MediaController`'s playback) seeking beyond its
     buffer issues a `Range`
     request, and answering it with a full `200` would make browsers restart the media
     at byte 0.
     SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS).
 - **SSR debug comments**: the host reads the `pathland.debug-html` property
   (`@Value("${pathland.debug-html:false}")`) and forwards it to each registry, enabling
   per-node HTML comments in SSR output when set.
 - **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `pathland.service-worker`
   (default `false`) forwards to the host; the SSR emits `data-pathland-service-worker`
   and the controller serves `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` +
   `Cache-Control: no-cache` (a stable, uncached script the browser byte-compares).
 - **`SpringConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketSession` to `PathlandConnection`.
   `AutoCloseable`: a failed send surfaces as a close (the session's
   `closeConnection` closes the underlying session) so the DOM client reconnects +
   `META::RESYNC` instead of silently stalling on an open socket.
 - **Heartbeat** — the socket replies to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
   **at the transport layer** (through its `SpringConnection`, no actor/session
   dependency; spec/OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat).
 - **Observability (issue #62)** — `spring-boot-starter-actuator` supplies the
   `MeterRegistry`; auto-config builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over it (decorated with
   `TracingTelemetry` when an `OpenTelemetry` bean is present — add
   `micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel` to opt in) and a `HealthIndicator` reporting the host
   UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/actuator/health`. The `pathland.*` meters are
   exposed at `/actuator/prometheus` (add `micrometer-registry-prometheus`).
 
 ## App DX
 
 ```java
 @SpringBootApplication
 public class MyApp {
     public static void main(String[] args) { SpringApplication.run(MyApp.class, args); }
     @Bean PathlandApp pathlandApp() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
     @Bean MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); } // optional 2nd app
 }
 ```
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `mvn test` — `PathlandAutoConfigurationTest` (`@SpringBootTest`): a `PathlandApp` bean
 mounts at `/` and SSR renders the root. `MultiSessionWebSocketTest`
 (`@SpringBootTest(RANDOM_PORT)`) opens **100 concurrent real WS sessions** against
 `/_pathland/ws` (via the shared `pathland-server-core` test-jar probe) and asserts each
 connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated, and is never closed by
 the peer. `PathlandObservabilityTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + `MockMvc`) asserts
 `/actuator/health` reports the `pathland` component UP and the auto-configured
 `PathlandTelemetry` is a `MicrometerTelemetry` registering `pathland.*` meters.
 `BaseCssHeadersTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + `MockMvc`) asserts the linked SSR
 `<link>`, the immutable `text/css` response at the global and mounted bases, and
 a 404 for an unknown hash.
 Manual: the `pathland-spring-boot-demo` renders `/`, `/kitchen`, `/settings`
 and the 404 fallback **and a second app at `/app2`**; a WebSocket handshake to
 `/_pathland/ws` and `/app2/_pathland/ws` returns 101.
\ No newline at end of file

 # Pathland Opcode Protocol Specification
 
 **Wire protocol version:** 1
 **Status:** Draft
 **Format:** Fixed-size (16-byte) opcode engine
 **Machine-readable IDs:** `spec/protocol.tsv`
 **Last Updated:** November 1, 2026
 
 ---
 
 ## Overview
 
 The Pathland Opcode Protocol is the **fixed-size instruction engine** at the heart of the Rust-first architecture. The **opcode engine** emits the application's **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment — as a stream of fixed 16-byte opcodes into a **ring buffer** in **linear memory**. The host renderer consumes the ring and maps the structure onto that platform's **native elements** (GTK4 widgets, DOM elements, HTML).
 
 **The engine does not compute layout and does not emit rects.** Native renderers lay out their own native elements from the constraint properties the engine passes through. This is the Pathland principle: *always render through that platform's native elements.*
 
 This specification supersedes the historical variable-length binary instruction format (which has been removed from the repository).
 
 The concrete numeric IDs are also emitted as the target-neutral `protocol.tsv`
 manifest from the canonical Rust constants; language bindings validate their
 hand-written constants against it. The prose tables remain authoritative for
 semantics, the manifest for exact wire numbers.
 
 ### Goals
 
 - **Sub-millisecond execution**: every opcode is a fixed 16 bytes; emission is a diff over the retained tree with **zero dynamic heap allocations** in the steady state.
 - **L1 CPU cache alignment**: a 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes**. Ring slots are 16-byte aligned and densely packed.
 - **Reactive emission**: only the nodes that changed emit opcodes. An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes (see [Reactive Emission](#reactive-emission)).
 - **Linear, deterministic decoding**: the host walks the ring with a single cursor.
 
 ### Core Principles
 
 1. **Fixed-size instructions**: every opcode is exactly 16 bytes — no length prefixes, no skippable-variable framing.
 2. **Declarative, not positioned**: the engine describes *what* the UI is (stacks, text, constraints), never *where* it is. Native elements compute their own positions.
 3. **Numeric IDs**: categories, commands, component types, and properties are numeric.
 4. **Native elements**: renderers map the opcode stream onto that platform's native elements — never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
 5. **Zero-copy**: the ring and arena are plain regions of the same linear memory shared with the host.
 6. **Single-producer / single-consumer**: the guest engine produces; the host renderer consumes. No locks required.
 
 ---
 
 ## Opcode Format
 
 Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**:
 
 ```
 [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
 ```
 
 | Field | Size | Offset | Description |
 |-------|------|--------|-------------|
 | `Category` | 1B | 0 | Opcode category (see [Category Table](#category-table)) |
 | `Command` | 1B | 1 | Command within the category (see [Command Tables](#command-tables)) |
 | `Flags` | 2B | 2 | Category/command-specific flags |
 | `A` | 4B | 4 | Primary payload |
 | `B` | 4B | 8 | Secondary payload |
 | `C` | 4B | 12 | Tertiary payload |
 
 All multi-byte values are **little-endian**. The Rust reference type is `#[repr(C, packed)]`:
 
 ```rust
 #[repr(C, packed)]
 pub struct Opcode {
     pub category: u8,
     pub command: u8,
     pub flags: u16,
     pub a: u32,
     pub b: u32,
     pub c: u32,
 }
 ```
 
 `size_of::<Opcode>() == 16`.
 
 ### Payload encoding conventions
 
 - **Float payloads** (`spacing`, `padding`, sizes) are stored as raw `f32` (IEEE 754) bit patterns in a `u32` field.
 - **Signed payloads** (the `I32` value type, and dedicated commands like `SET_DATE`'s days-since-epoch) are stored as the raw two's-complement bit pattern of a signed value in a `u32` field; a consumer reinterprets the field as `i32`.
 - **Node IDs** are `u32`.
 - **Component types / property IDs** are `u16`; when packed into a 4-byte payload they occupy the low two bytes (the high bytes are reserved / zero unless documented).
 - **Arena references** are a `u32` byte offset into the arena region (see [Arena](#arena)).
 - **Colors** are packed `0xAARRGGBB` in sRGB (see [Colors](#colors)).
 
 ### Reserved ranges
 
 - `Category == 0` is reserved (invalid).
 - `Command == 0` in any category is reserved (invalid).
 - `Category 0x80-0xFF`: custom/extended categories.
 
 ---
 
 ## Category Table
 
 | Category | Value | Name | Producer | Description |
 |----------|-------|------|----------|-------------|
 | `TREE` | `0x01` | Tree mutations | Guest engine | Node create/delete/insert/remove/move |
 | `PARAMETER` | `0x02` | Constraints & tokens | Guest engine | Property values (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |
 | `EVENT` | `0x03` | Raw inputs | Host renderer | Pointer down/move/up, key down/up |
 | `META` | `0x04` | Control | Both | Reset, environment, window metadata |
 
 ---

 | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
 |---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
 | `CREATE_NODE` | `0x01` | nodeId | componentType (u16, low) | 0 | — | Create a node of `componentType` |
 | `DELETE_NODE` | `0x02` | nodeId | 0 | 0 | — | Delete a node and its subtree |
 | `INSERT_CHILD` | `0x03` | parentId | childId | index | — | Insert `childId` into `parentId` at `index`; append is `index = u32::MAX` (`APPEND`) |
 | `REMOVE_CHILD` | `0x04` | parentId | childId | 0 | — | Remove `childId` from `parentId` |
 | `MOVE_CHILD` | `0x05` | parentId | childId | newIndex | — | Move child to `newIndex` (after removal); append is `newIndex = u32::MAX` (`APPEND`) |
 
 ### PARAMETER (0x02)
 
 The engine does not emit positions. `PARAMETER` carries the **constraint properties**
 that native renderers feed to their own layout — spacing, alignment, FILL/HUG
 size hints — plus **styling modifiers** (padding, colors, fonts, borders).
 
 | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
 |---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
 | `SET_PROPERTY` | `0x01` | nodeId | propertyId (u16, low) + valueType (u8, high byte) | value | — | Set a constraint/style property; `value` depends on `valueType` |
 | `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x02` | arenaRef (path) | valueType (u8) | value | — | Override a design token; path is an arena string |
 | `SET_TEXT` | `0x03` | nodeId | arenaRef (utf8) | 0 | — | Set a node's text content |
 | `SET_DATE` | `0x04` | nodeId | days since epoch (I32) | millis of day (U32) | — | Set a node's date value (e.g. a `DATE_PICKER`); see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md#date) for the matching `DATE_CHANGED` event |
 | `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` | `0x05` | nodeId | arenaRef (payload) | 0 | — | Set a node's text content plus style runs and links; payload format below |
 
 `SET_PROPERTY` encodes the value type in the **high byte of `B`** (bits 24–31) and the property id in the low two bytes:
 
 ```
 B = (valueType << 16) | propertyId
 ```
 
 #### Value types
 
 | Value Type | Value | C / value encoding |
 |------------|-------|--------------------|
 | `U8` | `0x01` | low byte of C |
 | `U32` | `0x02` | u32 |
 | `I32` | `0x03` | i32 |
 | `F32` | `0x04` | f32 |
 | `STRING` | `0x05` | arenaRef (utf8) |
 | `ENUM` | `0x06` | low byte of C |
 | `COLOR` | `0x07` | packed `0xAARRGGBB` |
 | `DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x08` | arenaRef (token path) |
 | `LIST` | `0x09` | arenaRef (length-prefixed array, see below) |
 
 > **Enum-valued properties** (`ALIGNMENT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`,
 > `ROLE`, `STATE`, and the draft `FONT_*`/`CONTENT_MODE`/`CONTROL_SIZE`/`SHAPE_KIND`
 > properties) are carried with the **`F32` value type**, holding the numeric enum
 > code as an f32 bit pattern (e.g. `ALIGNMENT=Center(1)` → `C = 1.0f32.to_bits()`).
 > The enumerated code tables live in
 > [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md#appendix-enumerated-values). The `ENUM` value type
 > (low byte of `C`) is available for explicitly `ENUM`-coded properties.
 >
 > **Token references**: any property that normally carries a `COLOR` / `F32` /
 > `STRING` / `ENUM` value MAY instead carry the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type, with
 > `C` = arenaRef to a token path (see [Design Token System](#design-token-system)
 > and [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md)).
 >
 > **`LIST` arrays**: a `LIST` value (`C` = arenaRef) is a length-prefixed array in
 > the string arena: `[u32 count][element × count]`, each element a `u32` holding
 > the value-type's bit pattern — currently produced with each element a `F32`
 > (the `FIT_QUERY` threshold table), so `bytes = 4 + 4·count`. The count is the
 > first `u32` (little-endian); a zero count is an empty list. Decoders read the
 > element count, never infer it from the arena length, so a property can re-emit
 > a shorter list with the arena entry intact.
 
 #### Attributed text payload (`SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`)
 
 `PARAMETER::SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` (`0x05`) sets a node's text together with
 range-scoped style runs and links. The opcode stays 16 bytes: `B` references a
 single length-prefixed arena entry (absolute offset over the shared ring,
 *relative* offset into the batch's string section over the network — the same
 dual convention as `SET_TEXT`). The payload is binary, not UTF-8:
 
 ```
 [u32 textByteLen][utf8 text]
 [u32 runCount]
   repeat runCount:
     [u32 start][u32 end][u32 attrCount]
     repeat attrCount:
       [u16 propId][u8 valueType][u8 reserved = 0][u32 value]
 [u32 linkCount]
   repeat linkCount:
     [u32 start][u32 end][u32 urlByteLen][utf8 url]
 ```
 
 All integers are little-endian. `start`/`end` are **UTF-8 byte offsets** into
 `text`, half-open `[start, end)`. A decoder MUST reject (ignore the opcode) when
 a range is not on a UTF-8 boundary or `end > textByteLen`.
 
 Style runs carry the **text-format property vocabulary** from
 [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md#2-text-formatting). V1 allows these scalar
 attributes only:
 
 | Property | ID | `valueType` | Value |
 |----------|----|-------------|-------|
 | `FONT_SIZE` | `0x1007` | `F32` (`0x04`) | points |
 | `FONT_WEIGHT` | `0x1008` | `F32` (`0x04`) | 100–900 |
 | `COLOR` | `0x100A` | `COLOR` (`0x07`) | `0xAARRGGBB` |
 | `FONT_STYLE` | `0x1017` | `F32` (`0x04`) | `Normal`=0, `Italic`=1 |
 | `FONT_DESIGN` | `0x1018` | `F32` (`0x04`) | `Default`=0, `Serif`=1, `Rounded`=2, `Monospaced`=3 |
 | `UNDERLINE` | `0x101F` | `U8` (`0x01`) | `0`/`1` |
 | `STRIKETHROUGH` | `0x1020` | `U8` (`0x01`) | `0`/`1` |
 
 `FONT_FAMILY` (`STRING`), `TEXT_STYLE`, `LINE_SPACING`, design-token references,
 and effects are **not** valid run attributes in v1 (runs carry scalar values
 only). A decoder ignores an unknown `propId` or unsupported `valueType`; it never
 errors the frame.
 
 Links are a separate section so style runs stay scalar-only. A link carries only
 its URL in v1; renderers own link presentation. Links and runs may overlap; the
 node's own text-format properties remain the base, and a run overrides the
 properties it sets for its range. Where multiple covering runs set the same
 property, the **later run in wire order wins**. Where multiple links cover a
 character, the later link wins.
 
 A renderer that does not implement rich text MUST still render the payload's
 `text` as plain text. The plain text is also the fallback when a payload fails
 validation. `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` supersedes `SET_TEXT` for the node: an engine
 that emits the attributed form does not also emit `SET_TEXT` for the same state.
 
 #### Constraint properties for native layout
 
 The following properties drive native layout; the renderer maps them to its
 native layout properties (e.g. `SPACING` → a gap between children,
 `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` → size requests). Special `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` values: `-1` = FILL
 (expand to available), `-2` = HUG_CONTENT (native intrinsic size).
 
 > **Allocation semantics** — the exact meaning of a Fixed / `FILL` / `HUG_CONTENT`
 > size, how containers distribute space to children (main axis: only `FILL`
 > expands; cross axis: children hug unless `FILL`), and how content fits inside
 > a Fixed box, are defined in [LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md).
 
 > **Units — logical points.** All size properties (`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`SPACING`/
 > `PADDING`/`CONTENT_MARGINS`, …) are expressed in an abstract **logical point**
 > unit — the same abstraction as SwiftUI points, Jetpack Compose `dp`, and CSS
 > pixels. A renderer MUST allocate the requested points box and fit content
 > within it; it must never treat the value as a device-pixel size. Each renderer
 > maps points to its native unit and resolves its own device resolution (logical
 > points × scale factor), so the same value yields the same physical size across
 > renderers.
 
 | Property | Value | Type | Native meaning |
 |----------|-------|------|----------------|
 | `SPACING` | `0x0001` | F32 | Gap between children |
 | `ALIGNMENT` | `0x0002` | F32 (enum code) | Cross-axis position (never stretches; default = Leading, `Fill`(3) = default hug — see LAYOUT.md) |
 | `CONTENT_MARGINS` | `0x0005` | F32 | Uniform inset between a stack's edge and its content |
 | `WIDTH` | `0x100B` | F32 | Width hint (-1 FILL, -2 HUG) |
 | `HEIGHT` | `0x100C` | F32 | Height hint (-1 FILL, -2 HUG) |
 | `GRID_COLUMNS` | `0x001E` | F32 | Grid column count (positive = count, -1/absent = auto-fit; a count, never a pixel width — see PRIMITIVES.md §Grid) |
 | `GRID_ROWS` | `0x001F` | F32 | Grid row count (positive = count, -1/absent = auto-fit) |
 | `GRID_TRACKS` | `0x0020` | STRING | Per-track grid spec (`flex`/`fixed:<pts>`/`adaptive:<pts>`, comma-separated) — takes precedence over the counts |
 
 #### Text properties
 
 Text-bearing nodes (`TEXT`, `BUTTON` labels, `TEXT_FIELD`) carry their content
 via `SET_TEXT` (0x03) and their layout via these properties:
 
 | Property | Value | Type | Native meaning |
 |----------|-------|------|----------------|
 | `TEXT` | `0x000A` | STRING | The text content (a `SET_TEXT`-style arena string) |
 | `LINE_LIMIT` | `0x000B` | U32 | Maximum number of lines (0 = unlimited) |
 | `TEXT_ALIGNMENT` | `0x000C` | F32 (enum code) | Alignment of the text block within its bounds |
 | `TRUNCATION_MODE` | `0x000D` | F32 (enum code) | Truncation style when text overflows (`Head`/`Middle`/`Tail`) |
 
 Enumerated values for these and every other enum-valued property are
 consolidated in [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md#appendix-enumerated-values).
 
 #### Styling properties (modifiers)
 
 Styling properties are **modifiers** — they apply to any view, not just stacks —
 and map to visual decoration rather than layout. `PADDING` (uniform) and its
 per-edge variants map to native padding, alongside
 `COLOR`/`BACKGROUND_COLOR`/`BORDER_*`:
 
 | Property | Value | Type | Native meaning |
 |----------|-------|------|----------------|
 | `PADDING` | `0x1011` | F32 | Uniform inner padding (any view) |
 | `PADDING_TOP` | `0x1012` | F32 | Top padding |
 | `PADDING_RIGHT` | `0x1013` | F32 | Right padding |
 | `PADDING_BOTTOM` | `0x1014` | F32 | Bottom padding |
 | `PADDING_LEFT` | `0x1015` | F32 | Left padding |
 | `BORDER_EDGES` | `0x1016` | U32 | Which border edges to draw (bitmask, see [`border_edges`] flags) |
 | `FIT_QUERY` | `0x1039` | LIST | A `SizeThatFits` slot's candidate fit-query: ascending `minWidth` thresholds (F32 elements) — the renderer measures its own allocated width and reports the fit index (see [`SizeThatFits`](./PRIMITIVES.md#size-that-fits--size-that-fits-0x17)) |
 | `TRANSITION` | `0x1031` | F32 (enum code) | Presentation hint for structural swaps (a `NavigationContainer` destination swap, a reactive component-body branch change): `None`=0, `PlatformDefault`=1, `Fade`=2, `Slide`=3, `Scale`=4 — the renderer **may** animate, never stores navigation state |
 
 `BORDER_EDGES` is a u32 bitmask (`SET_PROPERTY` with the `U32` value type)
 selecting which edges of a node's border are drawn. Bits are direction-aware:
 
 | Bit | Mask | Edge | Physical (LTR) |
 |-----|------|------|----------------|
 | 0 | `0x00000001` | `TOP` | top |
 | 1 | `0x00000002` | `LEADING` | left |
 | 2 | `0x00000004` | `BOTTOM` | bottom |
 | 3 | `0x00000008` | `TRAILING` | right |
 
 Full property catalog: see [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md) — the core modifiers
 (the protocol's `PARAMETER` properties) grouped by SwiftUI modifier, with the same
 IDs — and the Rust `constants.rs` (carried forward from the historical
 protocol).
 
 #### Semantic properties
 
 Semantic properties describe a node's meaning and interaction state rather than
 its layout or decoration. Currently exercised: `SELECTED` carries the boolean
 checked state of a `TOGGLE` (`SET_PROPERTY` with the `U8` value type, `0` = off,
 `1` = on). `EVENT_LISTENERS` (below) declares which raw inputs a node wants
 reported; `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID` identify bound callbacks that gate event
 delivery (see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md#transport-aware-event-guards-must)).
 
 | Property | Value | Type | Meaning |
 |----------|-------|------|---------|
 | `ROLE` | `0x2001` | ENUM (F32 code) | Accessibility role (see below) |
 | `STATE` | `0x2002` | ENUM (F32 code) | Control/interaction state (see below) |
 | `ENABLED` | `0x2003` | U8 | Whether the control is enabled |
 | `SELECTED` | `0x2004` | U8 | Checked/selected state of a `TOGGLE` |
 | `EVENT_LISTENERS` | `0x2005` | U32 | Bitmask of raw-input events to report |
 | `VALUE` | `0x2006` | F32 | Current value of a value-bearing control (e.g. `SLIDER`) |
 | `MIN_VALUE` | `0x2007` | F32 | Inclusive minimum of a `SLIDER`'s range |
 | `MAX_VALUE` | `0x2008` | F32 | Inclusive maximum of a `SLIDER`'s range |
 | `LABEL` | `0x200A` | STRING | Caption label of a `TEXT_FIELD` |
 | `PROMPT` | `0x200B` | STRING | Placeholder text of a `TEXT_FIELD` |
 | `ACTION_ID` | `0x2016` | U32 | Bound callback id; gates event delivery for this node |
 | `BINDING_ID` | `0x2017` | U32 | Two-way binding id (control value ↔ app state) |
 | `TOGGLE_STYLE` | `0x2018` | ENUM (F32 code) | Visual style token for a `TOGGLE`: `Switch`=0, `Checkbox`=1, `Button`=2 |
 | `ROUTE` | `0x2019` | STRING | Current navigation path (absolute, e.g. `/users/42`); drives web URL sync — see [DSL.md §4.5](./DSL.md#45-navigation) |
 | `NAV_DEPTH` | `0x201A` | U32 | Navigation back-stack depth (destinations in the app's path incl. current; `push`+1, `pop`−1, `replace` unchanged); lets native navigation adapters reconcile their page stack by depth — see [DSL.md §4.5](./DSL.md#45-navigation) |
 | `NAV_CHROME` | `0x201B` | F32 (enum code) | Navigation chrome mode on a `NavigationContainer` slot: `PlatformDefault`=0 (renderer supplies chrome — native container where one exists, renderer-drawn back affordance where none exists), `Custom`=1 (developer owns all nav UI; renderer adds none).  > checkbox, slider, toggle, menu, text field, …) are **not roles** — they are

 > expressed with `Button` + `ButtonStyle`. The renderer maps each semantic role
 > onto a semantically-structured native element; control components keep their
 > native element and never take an ARIA role from `ROLE`. **Headings** come from

 > defaults to a plain text element.
 
 **`STATE` enumerated values** (control/interaction state; carried as an `F32` numeric code, `value_type::F32`):
 
 | Value | State |

 | 2 | `Focused` |
